methods.label: Find the forced horizontal chain
methods.explanation:
Because rotating and reflecting are forbidden, a rectangle's right label must match its right neighbor's left label. Start with positions \(I,II,III\), since they require a chain of three rectangles.

[Figure 1](figures/1998_AMC_12_Q01_question_fig1.svg)

Checking the right label of each rectangle against all left labels gives exactly these possible left-to-right neighbors:
\[
B\to C\quad(3),\qquad D\to A\quad(4),\qquad E\to D\quad(7).
\]
Rectangle \(A\) has right label \(6\), and no rectangle has left label \(6\). Likewise, \(C\)'s right label \(5\) has no matching left label. Thus the displayed list includes every possible horizontal match. The only way to join two matches into a chain of three is
\[
E\to D\to A.
\]
Consequently positions \(I,II,III\) must contain \(E,D,A\), respectively.

To verify that this chain extends to a full arrangement, put \(B\) in position \(IV\) and \(C\) in position \(V\). The vertical matches are \(E\)'s bottom \(0\) with \(B\)'s top \(0\), and \(D\)'s bottom \(8\) with \(C\)'s top \(8\). The bottom horizontal match is \(B\)'s right \(3\) with \(C\)'s left \(3\). Every shared side matches, and every rectangle is used once. Position \(I\) contains rectangle \(\boxed{E}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
